questions.question: 1. What is a height balanced binary tree?

answers.a: A binary tree whose subtrees differ in height by at most one.
answers.c: Any binary tree whose subtrees differ in height by at least two.

explanations.a: Correct. A height balanced binary tree is defined as a tree where the left and right subtrees of every node differ in height by at most one.
explanations.b: Incorrect. While an empty tree is height balanced, it is not the only case.
explanations.c: Incorrect. If the height difference is two or more, the tree is not height balanced.

questions.question: 2. Height balanced binary trees cannot be used to avoid formation of skew trees.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Height balanced binary trees are specifically designed to prevent the formation of skew trees.
explanations.b: Correct. By maintaining a maximum height difference of one between subtrees, height balanced binary trees avoid skew trees, which have only one child or no child.

questions.question: 3. Which of the following is an AVL Tree?

answers.a: A self-balancing tree with at least 1 height difference.
answers.b: Any tree with exactly three children.
answers.c: A self-balancing tree with at most 3 height difference.
answers.d: A self-balancing tree with at most 1 height difference.

explanations.a: Incorrect. An AVL tree must have a height difference of at most 1 between subtrees.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The number of children does not determine if a tree is AVL.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A height difference greater than 1 violates the AVL property.
explanations.d: Correct. AVL trees are binary search trees that maintain a height difference of at most 1 between left and right subtrees.

questions.question: 4. An empty tree is height balanced.

explanations.a: Incorrect. An empty tree is height balanced because it has no subtrees, so the height difference is zero.
explanations.b: Correct. With no subtrees, an empty tree cannot violate the balance property, so it is height balanced.

questions.question: 5. If there are two different leaf nodes of an AVL tree, what is the maximum possible height difference between them?

answers.b: log(n), where n is the number of nodes
answers.c: n, where n is the number of nodes

explanations.a: Correct. In an AVL tree, the height difference between any two leaf nodes is at most 1, due to the balancing property.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The height difference is not logarithmic; it is at most 1.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The height difference is not linear in the number of nodes.

questions.question: 6. If an AVL tree has n nodes, then what will be its maximum height?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Let height of tree be 'H', then number of nodes which sum to n can be written in terms of height as N(H)=N(H-1)+1+N(H-2). Since N(H) which is 'n' can be written in terms of height as the beside recurrence relation which on solving gives N(H)= O(log n) as worst case height.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This would be the worst case for an unbalanced tree, not an AVL tree.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This is not the correct formula for AVL tree height.
explanations.d: Correct. Let height of tree be 'H', then number of nodes which sum to n can be written in terms of height as N(H)=N(H-1)+1+N(H-2). Since N(H) which is 'n' can be written in terms of height as the beside recurrence relation which on solving gives N(H)= O(log n) as worst case height.
